original_question: Does there exist an oracle x such that Ω^x >=_T 0′′, where Ω^x = sum_{sigma in 2^{<omega}} 2^{-K^x(sigma)} and K^x(sigma) = min{|tau| : U^x(tau) = sigma}?
target_in_paper: Section 4 (Liang Yu), Problem 6 (Downey–Hirschfeldt–Miller–Nies): Is there an x such that Omega^x >=_T 0'', where Omega^x = sum_{sigma in 2^{<omega}} 2^{-K^x(sigma)} and K^x(sigma) = min{|tau| : U^x(tau) = sigma}?
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation and in substance matches it almost verbatim: it asks for the existence of an oracle x with Omega^x >=_T 0'', and it gives the same displayed definitions of Omega^x and K^x(sigma) that appear in Problem 6.
missing_details: Make explicit that x ranges over reals/oracles, e.g. x in 2^omega (equivalently x subseteq omega).

Make explicit that U is the fixed machine used in the definition of K^x; to be fully stand-alone, one should say that U is the chosen universal prefix-free oracle machine underlying this version of K^x.
Spell out that >=_T means Turing reducibility (equivalently, Omega^x computes 0'').
Spell out that 0'' is the second Turing jump of the empty set.

Clarify that the question is about this specific Omega-operator determined by the fixed U in the definition, not a quantified statement over all universal machines and not an existence statement for a specially chosen U.

There are no extra algebraic ambient assumptions here (ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, etc.); the only hidden assumptions are computability-theoretic ones about the oracle x, the machine U, and Turing reducibility.
refined_question: Fix a universal prefix-free oracle machine U. For each oracle x in 2^omega and each finite binary string sigma in 2^{<omega}, define K^x(sigma) = min{|tau| : U^x(tau) = sigma}, and define Omega^x = sum_{sigma in 2^{<omega}} 2^{-K^x(sigma)}. Does there exist an oracle x such that Omega^x computes the second Turing jump of the empty set, i.e. Omega^x >=_T 0''?
justification: arXiv:2507.03972 is a workshop open-problems paper, and your draft targets the official open problem in Section 4, namely Problem 6, rather than a neighboring broader issue. The wording in your draft matches the paper's displayed statement almost exactly. The nearest paper-supplied context is Proposition 7 on the same page, which shows that for every y there exists x with Omega^x xor 0' >=_T y; this explains why the sharp paper-faithful question is whether one can obtain 0'' from Omega^x alone. Theorem 8 and Problem 9 are adjacent and motivate the surrounding discussion, but they do not supply an equivalent reformulation of Problem 6, so the refined question should remain exactly this existence question and no broader one.
